problem:
Consider the line $y=5x-2$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T?$

activity_context.topic_title: Linear Transformations of Points and Lines in the Plane

examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Image of a Line Given by an Equation in Slope-Intercept Form
examples.problem:
Consider the line $y=3x-2$ and linear transformation $\mathbf T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14055459/assets/3af646f67ee7157e5157ddd1d4296716e859c7d7c7c18d45037219ed4f75606e.png)

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $\mathbf T?$
examples.worked_solution:
First, let's find two points on the given line. Substituting $x=0$ and $x=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x=0\, & \to \,y=3(0)-2=-2, \\ x=1\, & \to \,y=3(1)-2=1.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have two points on the line, $P(0,-2)$ and $Q(1,1).$

To find the images of $P$ and $Q$ under the action of $\mathbf T,$ we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of $P$ and $Q$ in its columns:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14055459/assets/eaa950b7f0525109f33153dc28218222e1da17d7643281e9ac17776e87503784.png)

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $\mathbf T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are $P'(0,-2)$ and $Q'(-1,4).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through $P'$ and $Q'\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-2) & =\frac{4-(-2)}{-1-0}(x-0) \\ y+2 & =-6x \\ 6x+y+2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 3 \\ \sqrt{2} & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

What are the coordinates of the point ${K}^{′}$, the image of $K(\sqrt{2},-2)$ under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the image of $K$ under the action of $T$, we first create a column-vector $x$ containing the coordinates of $K:$

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $x$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $Tx:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Tx & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 3 \\ \sqrt{2} & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The result, $Tx,$ contains the coordinates of ${K}^{′}.$ Therefore, ${K}^{′}(-4,-8).$
